Management of malignant disease Carcinoid tumours and other secretory neo- plasms. All neoplastic cells have some abnormalities of metabolism, and many secrete characteristic metabolic products. Where the substance secreted has hormonal or pharmacological properties profound clinical effects may result, particularly since secretion is generally unregulated by normal homoeostatic mechanisms. Examples of syn- dromes associated with such secretory neoplasms include acromegaly (p.1798), Cushing’s syndrome (p.2344), hy- perprolactinaemia (p.2079), and other endocrine disorders associated with pituitary adenomas; phaeochromocytoma (p.1179); and carcinoid syndrome and the various syn- dromes associated with pancreatic endocrine tumours. Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) and type 2 (MEN2) are inherited conditions in which many tumours occur in often more than one endocrine organ; tumours in this disorder are often secretory.1,2 644 Antineoplastics Table 1.
